source.title: What Should LLMs Forget: Reinforcement Unlearning of Knowledge Associations
source.authors: Wu-Tong Xu; Yun Qu; Hai-Yan Feng; Qi Wang; Xiang-Yang Ji

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests recovery through adversarial prompting with its own attack benchmark and unlearning methods, rather than testing fine-tuning, activation ablation, or quantization recovery.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the RWKU adversarial-attack (AA) scores and the reported component-ablation AA scores. AA is described as attempting to elicit forgotten knowledge; the paper also explicitly calls the LF result improved robustness against paraphrased knowledge recovery. The paper does not report the AA prompt details or an unlearned model that never acquired the knowledge. Its cited claims about extraction and reactivation are not counted as results. The entropy and distribution-shift analyses do not test whether knowledge is stored but inaccessible rather than removed.
record.test_reason: KARU is a new unlearning method evaluated against RWKU's adversarial-attack (AA) probe, which tries to elicit forgotten knowledge by prompting, and is compared with other methods. This bears on F (resistance to prompting attacks). The attack prompts are not described. The paper never frames AA as recovery relative to direct probes, so it does not cleanly test E. It runs no fine-tuning, activation-ablation or quantization attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that KARU improves forgetting and the forget–retain trade-off across models and RL algorithms while keeping comparable retention and utility. They credit logits flattening with the lowest AA scores and with improved robustness to paraphrased recovery. They do not claim robustness to other attacks.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces KARU, an RL framework with token-level rewards, logits flattening, and adaptive neighborhood sampling. It evaluates adversarial prompting but does not apply the fine-tuning, activation-ablation, or quantization recovery procedures in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: AA outcomes vary by model, optimizer, and KARU component: on Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, PPO KARU has a higher AA score than RULEPPO, whereas GRPO KARU has a lower score than RULEGRPO; component ablations also produce different AA scores.

fits_no_version.finding: KARU gives higher predictive entropy at knowledge-token positions than RT and RULE across RWKU subsets (Fig. 7). Fictitious knowledge has higher entropy than memorized knowledge (Fig. 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entropy-based confidence measure of forgotten knowledge, not a measure of recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: Distribution shifts after unlearning concentrate on knowledge tokens. KL at knowledge positions is 0.770 for RULE and 1.133 for KARU (Appendix A).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Localization of the unlearning-induced distribution shift.

record.problems: The AA prompt construction and attack-set size are not stated in the supplied text. The AA results use ROUGE-L recall and do not compare against a model that never acquired the target knowledge, so they cannot establish how much knowledge was recovered relative to that reference. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the AA results.

untested.parts: There is no comparison to chance-level accuracy or to a never-trained model. The general-capability metrics are reported, but no claim of near-chance forgetting is tested.
No activation ablation. The entropy analyses do not test whether knowledge is blocked or deleted.
No separate rephrase, jailbreak, cross-lingual or in-context conditions are reported. The AA prompt details are not given, and AA is not compared with direct probes as a measure of recovery.
Resistance to fine-tuning, activation ablation and quantization is not tested. MUSE has no attack probe.

missing.what: FB and QA (non-attack) forget scores for every method. Within each model AA exceeds QA (e.g. KARU-PPO QA 13.5 vs AA 32.5; RULE-GRPO QA 23.7 vs AA 41.1). This is a possible but probe-set-confounded signal of prompting recovery.
MUSE results (no attack probe). KARU-PPO has No Know Mem. 0.0 and utility 30.3, against 71.0 for the original model.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's version labels V5/V6 map to E/F. Duplicate ablation rows (r35, r38, r39, r42) have been unlinked. No E verdict is given because the rows only compare AA with the original model. The text's FB/QA-vs-AA comparison is not on a matched probe set. KARU is initialized from a rejection-tuned model, so its low scores partly reflect refusal behaviour. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports forgetting and general-capability measures, but does not establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy or compare attack recovery with a model that never acquired the knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation is tested, and the distribution analyses do not establish that the method blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
No weight quantization attack is tested.

Tests RWKU adversarial attacks, including an explicitly described paraphrased-recovery assessment, but not jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information. Attack prompt details are not stated.
KARU is evaluated against the RWKU adversarial-prompt attack only; resistance to fine-tuning, activation ablation, and quantization is not tested.

relation.reason: Reports AA results for its own method against baselines, which bear on F.

tranche.reason: A new RL unlearning method, evaluated on RWKU's adversarial-attack (prompting) probe against baselines.

source_check.notes: AA is RWKU's adversarial prompting probe only; the paper never describes the attack prompts. No relearning, quantization or activation-edit attacks are tested, and the MUSE appendix has none. Table 3's model is not named; its baselines match Table 1 Llama3-8B RULE, and its rows are RULE+components, not partial KARU. KARU starts from the RT model (RT AA: 51.6 on 8B, 49.2 on 3B). Table 2's text is column-scrambled, but the values place by the aggregate checks.

statements.correction: KARU RWKU AA (ROUGE-L recall, lower is better): Llama3.2-3B PPO 39.2 vs GRPO 29.3 (optimizer, same backbone); Qwen2.5-7B PPO 30.1, GRPO 31.1; Llama3-8B PPO 32.5, GRPO 34.0.
statements.problem: The statement cites KARU rows r24 and r25 but says nothing about KARU. Both rows use the same backbone (Llama3.2-3B) and differ only in optimizer, so they do not show the stated factor (base model family, backbone, dataset and split).
